issue.title: [8.x] Compare custom date/immutable_date using date comparison
issue.body:
### Description:

Model attributes cast as custom date(time) formats are incorrectly marked as dirty attributes when the value has not in fact changed.

I first noticed this happening as part of a Livewire controller, but it’s not limited to just Livewire.

### Steps To Reproduce:

See #38719 for some steps.

Most basic example:

https://github.com/macbookandrew/laravel-bug-report/blob/e44c1422b154b02bb59c2aedae3c9ce45798bc2d/tests/Feature/EventDateTest.php#L41

### Cause

The `HasAttributes` `originalIsEquivalent` method does not treat custom date/immutable_date attributes as date objects and does a strict comparison; if the Carbon instance has changed, it fails.

### Suggested solution

If an attribute `isDateCastable()` then compare them using `fromDateTime()` rather than creating new Carbon instances and comparing them.

body: Also, if the $dateFormat property is specified, then in version 8.60, if there was a caste on the field, then this format was ignored and taken from the caste attributes. In version 8.61, the caste attributes are ignored and the $dateFormat property is always used.
I agree, since 8.61 $dateFormat or grammar's default date format have priority over custom caster format. In fact, caster format is never used anymore.

Last week's pull request fixed `Model@setAttribute()` falsely marking an attribute as dirty when assigning  `Carbon` objects for the same timestamp. However the new test case added didn't have coverage for assigning date strings which is the common use case when `$request->validated()` is filled into the model. Before, assigned raw date strings were left as-in in the `Model@attributes` payload but now they're reformatted by `setAttribute()` / `fromDateTime()`.

Two potential `setAttribute()` fixes:

1. https://github.com/laravel/framework/compare/8.x...derekmd:fix-set-attribute-custom-cast-date-format-string-value?expand=1
  This keeps the v8.60.0 behavior by not modifying string values assigned to date-casted attributes. The solution is hacky as it's partially undoing the last pull request.
2. https://github.com/laravel/framework/compare/8.x...derekmd:fix-setattribute-custom-cast-date-format?expand=1
  This ultimately fixes the dirty state behavior where you can assign any date string, `DateTimeInterface`, or `Carbon` object and always have attribute value comparisons work. The SQL binding value will match the expected `date`/`datetime`/`immutable_date`/`immutable_datetime` cast format. However in a patch release this would affect test suite feedback and it contradicts [current 8.x docs](https://laravel.com/docs/8.x/eloquent-mutators#date-casting):
   
   > When defining a date or datetime cast, you may also specify the date's format. This format will be used when the model is serialized to an array or JSON

   Now the date format would also be used for model attribute assignment and SQL bindings.

Unless a better patch-level solution can be thought up for bullet point 1, I think https://github.com/laravel/framework/pull/38720 should be reverted and the fix should be made in 9.x.
Probably have to revert. Might make it a policy to reject all changes to casting / "is dirty" behavior.

issue.title: [8.x] - fix for custom date castable and database value formatting
issue.body:
This is a followup to #38720 and #38828.

Instead of always treating `custom_datetime` and `immutable_custom_datetime` casts as `isDateCastable()`, this only checks them in the `originalIsEquivalent()` method.

This retains the old behavior for formatting values for the database, while incorporating a fix to ensure that custom (immutable) date casts are compared correctly, even if the Carbon instance is not identical.
